skill.name: polars
skill.description: Use Polars for fast DataFrame workflows, including lazy queries, expression-based transformations, joins, aggregations, and CSV or Parquet I/O.

content.value_statement: Large tabular workflows can become slow and hard to maintain. This skill helps users design efficient Polars pipelines with clear patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains Polars expressions for selecting, filtering, and deriving columns.
Shows lazy evaluation patterns for large CSV and Parquet workflows.
Maps common pandas operations to Polars equivalents.
Covers joins, concatenation, pivots, unpivots, and list transformations.
Provides guidance for database, cloud storage, and file format I/O.
Highlights performance practices for streaming, pushdown, and data types.
limitations: Does not execute Polars queries or inspect datasets by itself.
Does not manage credentials, permissions, or cloud storage accounts.
Version-specific Polars behavior may require checking official documentation.
Examples may need adaptation for production schemas and data volumes.

use_cases.title: Build Faster Batch Pipelines
use_cases.description: Design lazy Polars workflows that read large files, filter early, aggregate data, and write efficient outputs.

use_cases.title: Migrate Pandas Analysis
use_cases.description: Translate familiar pandas selection, grouping, joining, and reshaping patterns into Polars expressions.

use_cases.title: Prepare Feature Tables
use_cases.description: Create repeatable transformations for joins, windows, categorical columns, and typed feature datasets.

prompt_templates.title: Load and Filter Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Polars plan for loading a CSV, selecting three columns, filtering rows, and exporting Parquet.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Pandas Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Translate my pandas grouping and join workflow into Polars, and explain each API difference briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Large File Processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Polars pipeline for lazy execution, predicate pushdown, streaming, and memory-efficient data types.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a production Polars workflow that reads partitioned Parquet, validates schema, performs joins, and writes partitioned results.

output_examples.input: Ask for a Polars approach to process a large CSV file.
output: A step-by-step plan using lazy scanning and early column selection.
Recommended filters, aggregations, and output format choices.
Notes about streaming and schema checks for large datasets.

output_examples.input: Ask to migrate a pandas grouping workflow to Polars.
output: A mapping from pandas operations to Polars expressions.
Warnings about parallel execution and expression context differences.
A test checklist for comparing row counts, schemas, and aggregates.

output_examples.input: Ask how to reshape data for reporting.
output: A recommended pivot or unpivot strategy based on the desired table shape.
Guidance on aggregation choices and duplicate keys.
Performance notes for filtering before reshaping.

best_practices: Use lazy scans for large files so Polars can optimize reads and filters.
Prefer native expressions over Python functions for parallel execution.
Choose Parquet and explicit data types for repeatable, efficient pipelines.
anti_patterns: Do not use eager reads for large datasets when lazy scans can reduce work.
Do not rely on row iteration for transformations that expressions can handle.
Do not place real credentials directly in example code or shared notebooks.

faq.question: What is Polars best at?
faq.answer: Polars is best for fast tabular data processing with expressions, lazy execution, and efficient file I/O.

faq.question: Can this skill replace pandas knowledge?
faq.answer: It helps translate pandas patterns, but users still need to validate behavior against their data.

faq.question: Does the skill run data jobs?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that users can adapt in their own environment.

faq.question: Does it cover cloud storage?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents S3, Azure, and Google Cloud Storage access patterns at a high level.

faq.question: Is lazy evaluation always required?
faq.answer: No. Eager mode is fine for small data, quick checks, and simple interactive work.

faq.question: How should users handle credentials?
faq.answer: Users should follow their platform security policy and avoid committing real credentials to files.
